defects.title: AC-C5 and AC-0.3 grep '^-[^-]' misses deleted bullets and --- lines
defects.quote: git diff -U0 master...HEAD -- src/superclaude/commands/<name>.md \| grep -E '^-[^-]'` | prints nothing: edits are additive
defects.what_goes_wrong: A removed markdown bullet '- x' appears in git diff -U0 as '-- x' (and a removed '---' as '----'), which '^-[^-]' skips, so the additive-edit gate prints nothing and passes while existing bullets or frontmatter lines are deleted, leaving SA-1/SA-4/SA-5 unenforced (reproduced in a scratch git repo: baseline '- keep','- gone','---', branch keeps only '- keep' -> diff shows '-- gone' and '----', grep prints nothing, exit 1).
defects.is_fixed_when: The AC-C5 and AC-0.3 commands (or their replacement) report non-empty/failing output for any deleted line whose text starts with '-' (e.g. a removed '- bullet' or '---'), excluding only the '--- a/...' file-header line, for example via grep -E '^-' | grep -vE '^--- ' or a git diff --numstat deleted-count of 0.
defects.deletion_note: No: deleting AC-C5/AC-0.3 would leave SA-4 and SA-5 ('additive', 'no existing routing row changed') with no mechanical check; the pass condition must stay and the pattern be corrected.
defects.present_in_others_hint: Same pattern appears at AC-0.3 (line 193); SA-4 (149) and SA-5 (150) rely on both; any later copy of the pattern in a revised spec.

defects.title: AC-C1 grep alternation written with \| (table escape) said to match nothing
defects.what_goes_wrong: Claimed: in raw grep -E '\|' is a literal bar, so AC-C1 never matches (true if pasted raw: reproduced), but the spec is a GFM table where '\|' is the standard cell escape rendered as '|', used identically in AC-C4, AC-C5, AC-0.3 and the pipeline '\| grep -v', so check (b) fails: a reader of the rendered table gets a working command.
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-C1 as an executable command contains an unescaped alternation that matches a planted 'orca orchestration check' line (only relevant if the spec is consumed as raw text rather than rendered markdown).
defects.deletion_note: No: removing AC-C1 would drop the only mechanical check of SA-2/WC-8.
defects.present_in_others_hint: All table-embedded shell commands using '\|' (AC-C4, AC-C5, AC-0.3, AC-1.x) share the same convention; a raw-text consumer would need all of them unescaped.

defects.title: AC-C1 scans core, where P0 writes Orca-mentioning contract and routing section
defects.quote: The only allowed mention of Orca in a changed command is as an example of a caller's question channel inside the contract file.
defects.what_goes_wrong: AC-C1 must print nothing over src/superclaude/core (excluding only ccsession-tag) in every phase, yet P0 adds WORKER-CONTRACT.md and an Orca section to HOW-WE-WORK.md in core and SA-2 permits an Orca mention in the contract file, so any 'orca orchestration/worktree/terminal/agent' wording there fails AC-C1 and the spec neither exempts those files nor forbids such wording.
defects.is_fixed_when: AC-C1 explicitly exempts WORKER-CONTRACT.md and the HOW-WE-WORK.md Orca section (or narrows its scan to command, skill and agent files), or SA-2/P0 state that those files must avoid the 'orca <subcommand>' text AC-C1 matches.
defects.deletion_note: No: dropping src/superclaude/core from the scan or removing AC-C1 would only be a fix if SA-2's scope is restated to match; deleting the contract file or Orca section would remove P0's deliverable.
defects.present_in_others_hint: SA-2 (147), P0 row (158), SA-5 (150) Orca section in routing guide and its two mirrored copies (plugins/superclaude/skills/sc-recommend/refs/HOW-WE-WORK.md, src/superclaude/core/CLAUDE.md level table), AC-0.2.
